author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Firefighters from East Providence and Rehoboth completed a 110-story memorial stair climb Friday at City View Manor, honoring first responders who died during the September 11 attacks. It was the first year the neighboring Rhode Island and Massachusetts departments organized the climb together.

Participants climbed the building's 11 flights ten times while wearing nearly 60 pounds of protective equipment. The repeated ascent matched the height of the World Trade Center towers and gave the public a physical reminder of the conditions firefighters faced. Families and community members gathered at the property to watch and support the crews as they worked through the heat.

Organizers said they hope the joint climb becomes an annual tradition. Donations associated with the event support the Tunnel to Towers Foundation, which assists injured service members, first responders and families of those killed in the line of duty. The collaboration also linked two local departments whose members regularly train for high-rise rescues and other emergencies. Friday's event focused on remembrance, shared service and the continuing impact of September 11 on fire departments across New England.
dek: Crews from East Providence and Rehoboth climbed the equivalent of 110 stories in nearly 60 pounds of gear.
headline: East Providence and Rehoboth firefighters complete 110-story memorial climb
